memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh and generate-context-line-counts.sh both refuse to run directly from the agent-system/extensions/core/scripts source-store path -- they require invocation from a deployed scripts/ tree (.claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/) because their own relative '../..' repo-root resolution assumes that location. Both scripts still read/validate against the SOURCE STORE (agent-system/extensions/**) once invoked correctly -- generate-context-line-counts.sh's own header explains this is deliberate (index-entries.json is source-of-truth, .claude/context/index.json is a disposable deploy artifact). Practical fix: run 'bash .claude/scripts/<name>.sh' (the already-deployed copy) rather than the source-store path, after confirming via diff -q that the deployed copy matches the source (no edit needed if they're already in sync).

index-entries.json's 'summary' field has a hard 200-character maxLength in core/context/index.schema.json, but nothing in the authoring workflow enforces it at write time -- an implementer summarizing a dense context file (Zotero integration, sparse-coverage detection, safety invariants) can easily exceed 200 chars without any error until a jsonschema/ajv validation pass catches it. Always run a schema validation pass (e.g. python3 jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(...).iter_errors(d)) over any index-entries.json touched during a task, even when check-extension-docs.sh itself passes -- Rule U only checks EXTENSION.md line count, not index-entries.json schema conformance.

Two @-pointer conventions coexist in agent-system/extensions/*/EXTENSION.md's Context Pointers sections: a bare relative form (@context/project/{ext}/...) used by literature/present/cslib/nix/web, and a '.claude/'-prefixed form (@.claude/context/project/{ext}/...) used by the pre-existing nvim extension and (as of this task) email. generate_claudemd() in merge.lua concatenates EXTENSION.md content verbatim into .claude/CLAUDE.md with NO path rewriting, so whichever form is written in source is exactly what a reader/loader sees. Since .claude/CLAUDE.md itself lives at .claude/CLAUDE.md (not repo root), Claude Code's own @-import resolution for content already injected as 'project instructions' appears to favor paths relative to CLAUDE.md's own directory (i.e. treating 'context/...' as '.claude/context/...'), which would make the bare form the actually-working one and the '.claude/'-prefixed form doubly-nested and non-resolving -- but this was not conclusively proven, only observed indirectly (nix's bare-form pointers had their target file contents auto-loaded into a session transcript; nvim/email's .claude/-prefixed pointers did not, though task-relevance could also explain that difference).
